newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Tyumentelekom plans ADR issue in September.
newsitem.headline: Tyumentelekom plans ADR issue in September.

text.p: Regional Russian telecoms company Tyumentelekom plans to launch a level-one American Depositary Receipts (ADR) programme on its ordinary and preferred shares at the beginning of September, a senior company official said on Thursday.

Tyumentelekom, traded on the Russian Trading System's RTS-2 market for less liquid stocks, expects to receive permission from the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for the issue by August 10, the company's economics director, Nadezhda Kapelistaya, told Reuters.

"Tyumentelekom plans to issue ADRs not only on ordinary shares, as was previously announced, but also on preferred stock," Kapelistaya said. "We will begin the placement at the beginning of September, when market activity picks up."

Tyumentelekom ordinaries closed on RTS-2 on Wednesday at $5.00. The preferred shares are not traded on RTS-2. Regional telecom companies are considered one of the most promising sectors of the Russian market and Tyumentelekom is actively traded considering its limited liquity.
Preferred shares account for 25 percent of Tyumentelekom's capital. The company plans a road-show to present its shares in September in New York, London and Boston, she said.

Kapelistaya said the ADR programme would not be limited. Previously the company had said it would cover 10 percent of its shares. The company is also considering a level-three ADR programme, she said.
